etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin vibrātus, perfect passive participle of vibrō (“agitate, set in tremulous motion”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyp- (“to oscillate, swing”) or *weyb-.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To shake with small, rapid movements to and fro.

quote.citation: 1837, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], “The Coronation”, in Ethel Churchill: Or, The Two Brides. […], volume II, London: Henry Colburn, […], →OCLC, page 5:
quote.text: When "God save the King!" resounded through the stately abbey, the banners vibrating with the mighty music, I felt quite enthusiastic in my loyalty.

quote.citation: 1951 October, R. S. McNaught, “Lines of Approach”, in Railway Magazine, page 706:
quote.text: The tender roared along vibrating vigorously; braking had resulted in "flats" on most of its tyres.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To brandish; to swing to and fro.
(transitive) To mark or measure by moving to and fro.
(transitive) To affect with vibratory motion; to set in vibration.

quote.citation: 1669, William Holder, Elements of Speech: An Essay of Inquiry into the Natural Production of Letters: […], London:  […]  T. N[ewcomb] for J[ohn] Martyn printer to the R[oyal] Society, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Breath vocalized, i.e., vibrated or undulated, may  […]  impress a swift, tremulous motion.

quote.citation: 1864, Alfred Tennyson, “Aylmer’s Field”, in Enoch Arden, &c., London: Edward Moxon & Co., […], →OCLC, page 81:
quote.text: Star to star vibrates light: may soul to soul / Strike thro' a finer element of her own?

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang, dated) To please or impress someone.

quote.text: And if he wants to give you high praise, he'll answer, "That vibrates me"; "That has a large charge"; or "That's oogley."

[…]  standing side by side under a Grecian column, tapping their feet in unison and saying such things as "Hot-diggety,” “Razz-ma-tazz," “That vibrates me," and other expressions of praise current in their youth.

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang) To pleasure someone using a vibrator.

quote.citation: 1999 March 27, PeterW, “Jack with Jill”, in alt.jokes.limericks‎[1] (Usenet):
quote.text: Downstairs in the living-room JillWas vibrating herself for a thrill.

definitions.definition: The setting, on a portable electronic device, that causes it to vibrate rather than sound any (or most) needed alarms.
